criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and community sanitation and drinking-water service access via two of four studied CSR rural development areas: construction of toilets (household, school, and public toilets) and construction/repair of water service infrastructure (tube wells, borewells, overhead tanks, and piped water supply).
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain broad wording of Criterion 2 because it examines corporate rural infrastructure provision mandated under India's Companies Act, 2013 (2% CSR spending mandate under Schedule VII), state CSR portal reporting categories, and corporate-state implementation partnerships. Fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading because the statutory CSR spending mandate operates only as macro-level funding/reporting background, while the empirical analysis of water and sanitation evaluates generic CSR infrastructure project delivery (construction quality, absence of water supply to toilets, digging borewells without checking groundwater levels, lack of maintenance, and lack of community consultation or awareness) rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household service access (such as eligibility screening, documentation or tenure requirements, administrative burden, tariffs/cost-recovery rules, enforcement, or utility regulatory structure).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary qualitative/field empirical evidence (interviews, focus group discussions, and field observations with 264 randomly sampled beneficiary households across 8 villages in Koraput district, Odisha) combined with secondary CSR expenditure data from the Odisha State CSR Portal (Go Care) and company annual reports (2014-2020).
criterion_notes.c4: Reports qualitative household and village-level outcomes relevant to sanitation access/use (continued open defecation vs toilet use due to missing piped water connections and poor construction quality) and drinking-water availability and reliability (dysfunctional piped water systems and defunct borewells/tubewells forcing reliance on river and stream water).
criterion_notes.c5: Identifies population and sample (264 randomly selected beneficiary households across 8 villages in HAL Koraput and NALCO Damanjodi CSR areas in Koraput district, Odisha), exposure (CSR rural infrastructure projects and expenditure under the Companies Act, 2013 from 2014-2020), outcomes (CSR financial allocations and qualitative beneficiary narratives/assessments of infrastructure functionality and use), and study design (mixed-methods empirical field study combining secondary portal data with household interviews and focus group discussions).

evidence_quotes.quote: So far, as rural development projects are concerned, four specific people-centric intervention projects, i.e., the construction of roads, installation of solar lights, construction of toilets and drinking water provision, have been brought into analysis and discussion.

The Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) guidelines floated through the Companies Act, 2013 made it mandatory for CSR units to engage in rural development activities notified in Scheduled VII of the Act.
Major reasons behind the shortfall of the programmes include low-quality infrastructure, lack of need assessment, awareness, maintenance, proprietor and community participation.

This empirical data has been collected from the sample beneficiary households through interviews and focus group discussions, coupled with the field experiences and notes prepared during his field visits and observation.

It has been found from the study areas that corporate constructed toilets at the backside of houses without any water supply system nearby. The villagers of Kapsiput cited the difficulty to collect water from open water sources located far away in the absence of piped water supply, and added that most of them, thereby, prefer open defecation.

The overhead water tank and piped water supply system at Kapsiput villages have not been functional since its construction. People depend on river and stream water, which is muddy, unhygienic, and unsafe.

raw_response.exposure: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) rural infrastructure projects and expenditures by HAL Koraput and NALCO Damanjodi under the Companies Act, 2013 (2014-2020)
raw_response.outcome: Functionality, quality, and household/community use of CSR-constructed toilets and drinking-water infrastructure (piped water systems, overhead tanks, borewells, tube wells), alongside district CSR expenditure allocations
raw_response.population_and_sample: 264 randomly selected beneficiary households across 8 purposively selected villages (4 each in HAL Koraput and NALCO Damanjodi CSR areas) in Koraput district, Odisha, India
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification. While the study empirically examines CSR-funded rural toilet construction and drinking-water infrastructure across eight villages in Koraput, Odisha, the legal reference to the Companies Act, 2013 (2% mandatory CSR spending and portal reporting categories) functions as macro-level corporate funding background, and the village-level water and sanitation analysis evaluates generic CSR project delivery (poor construction quality, lack of water supply to toilets, unmaintained pipes/borewells, and absence of community consultation or awareness) rather than any rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism governing household service access. Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, it would be included.
raw_response.study_design: Mixed-methods cross-sectional empirical study combining secondary CSR expenditure portal analysis (2014-2020) with multistage stratified/random household interviews, focus group discussions, and field observations
